title: Enterprise account churn (ambiguous)
research_question: Why did the enterprise account most likely churn?
analyst_instructions: The evidence packet supports more than one defensible account of the cause. Do not try to guess a single intended answer. Record what you actually believe and why, including any unknowns.
reviewer_instructions: Expect at least one pair of units where the two analysts assert genuinely incompatible causes. Only tag 'contradiction' if both cannot be true simultaneously given the evidence — a difference in emphasis is not a contradiction.
baseline_prose_instructions: Same as Case 1: give the reviewer only the raw prose write-ups for the baseline condition.
expected_methodological_risks: Reviewers may be tempted to resolve the ambiguity themselves rather than report it — the rubric term for this is 'accurate but low value' only if both units are individually true; if the two claims cannot both be true, it is a contradiction, not a low-value event.
This case has no single correct answer. Do not grade divergences against a hidden key.
design_note_do_not_show_before_grading: Analyst A's evidence trail leans toward a pricing-driven churn; Analyst B's leans toward a support-quality-driven churn. Both use E2 (the exit survey). Both cite the same evidence for opposite proximate causes — this is the intended 'divergent_conclusion_shared_evidence' and, if the reviewer judges the two claims mutually exclusive, a genuine reviewer-confirmed contradiction.
